tagline: Namibia's deep-water harbour and marine-tourism gateway — a flamingo lagoon, a seal-colony spit and a road-less desert harbour.
summary: Walvis Bay is Namibia's principal port, set on a natural deep-water harbour sheltered by the Pelican Point sand spit. The bay holds a Ramsar-listed lagoon famous for its flamingos, a seal and dolphin colony at Pelican Point, and — down a road-less desert coast to the south — the dramatic dune-and-lagoon landscape of Sandwich Harbour. The resort town of Swakopmund lies a short way up the coast to the north. A well-established cruise-and-kayak tour trade already departs the Walvis Waterfront, proving durable marine-tourism demand.

demand_signals.note: Namibia's main coastal resort town lies ~30km north; a coastal water link connects the two poles.

demand_signals.note: The Pelican Point spit and lagoon geography make several points slow to reach overland.

use_cases.title: Seal-colony bay run
use_cases.body: A scheduled run from the Walvis Waterfront around the Pelican Point spit to the seal colony upgrades the existing cruise trade with a fast, quiet craft.

use_cases.title: Road-less desert harbour
use_cases.body: A coastal service south to Sandwich Harbour reaches a landscape with no road access, today limited to 4x4 convoys and small boats.

use_cases.title: Resort coastal link
use_cases.body: A coastal run north to Swakopmund connects Namibia's port and its main resort town by water.

use_cases.title: Lagoon & port hop
use_cases.body: Short hops across the bay and lagoon serve port and waterfront points faster than the road loop.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Ideal for the bay and lagoon hops and the coastal runs to Sandwich Harbour (~26nm) and Swakopmund (~17nm), all inside Pioneer range, where sheltered water behind Pelican Point and short legs favour a fast, clean craft.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Reserved for any longer coastal extensions along the Skeleton Coast, where range matters more than frequency.

transit_planning: Namibia's coastal transport centres on the Walvis Bay port expansion and the coastal road to Swakopmund; passenger water services are tourism-operator led, leaving room for a scheduled, bookable tier that also serves point-to-point coastal links.

competitive_landscape: Walvis Bay already supports a mature cruise-and-kayak operator trade from the waterfront, proving marine-tourism demand; there is no fast, scheduled point-to-point water service, so a foiling tier both upgrades the tour product and adds coastal links (Sandwich Harbour, Swakopmund) that road cannot serve well.
seasonality: The Benguela coast is cool, foggy and largely rain-free year-round, with strong afternoon winds common; mornings offer the calmest water, and the bay behind Pelican Point stays sheltered, supporting a long operating window.
regulatory_note: Marine activity falls under the Namibian Ports Authority (Namport) and maritime affairs; the lagoon's Ramsar wetland status means clean, low-wake, zero-emission operation is a strong environmental fit for scheduled service.

precedents.why_it_matters: Proves durable, year-round demand for water-based tourism a faster clean craft can capture and grow.
Shows premium demand for a destination only water or 4x4 can reach, ideal for a scheduled water link.
